attribution: Framed as a teaching of the sage Yajnavalkya to Gargi; actual author unknown, and several different works share the title
period: Dating is debated; proposals range widely, with some scholars placing the main text in the early second millennium CE
summary: A dialogue-based yoga text that sets an eightfold yoga, with detailed breathwork, inside a Vedic and Vedantic frame.
whyRead: It shows yoga being taught as part of orthodox Vedic life rather than in a renunciant or tantric setting, and it is notable for having a woman, Gargi, as the questioner.
story: The text is framed as Yajnavalkya instructing Gargi, a learned woman, in the eight limbs of yoga.
questions: How was yoga integrated into Vedic householder life?
What role does breath play in meditation?

keyTeachings.title: An eightfold yoga
keyTeachings.text: Like the Yoga Sutras it teaches eight limbs, but it develops them in its own way, with long lists of ethical restraints and observances and many postures and breath practices.

keyTeachings.title: Breath and the vital winds
keyTeachings.text: It gives a detailed account of the vital airs (prana and others) and channels, and of pranayama as purification.

keyTeachings.title: A Vedantic goal
keyTeachings.text: The aim is described in terms of knowing the self and its unity with Brahman, joining yoga to Vedanta.
